# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document accompanies
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC’s phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> RFC-039’s main text is the sole authority for phase order and acceptance gates. This document only
> decomposes the work into executable granularity and records conflicts that have not yet been
> adjudicated.

## Scope and Positioning

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one to RFC-039’s phase sequence                                     |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each able to form and archive a team independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                      |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, P8 has no `8.1`; after withdrawal of the
LALRPOP route, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` are also unused (2026-11-25). None of the three has had a
corresponding entry since the WBS was established: all revisions of this document have zero matches
for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can verify this), and there
are no references elsewhere in the repository. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test
revival and completion). That phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`; therefore, P8’s
numbering is aligned with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered here**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallel groups, and binding acceptance
criteria.

**Not covered here**: design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or justification for phase ordering
(see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered level-2/level-3 rows **must
contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P to which the task truly belongs, which may differ
from its containing section) and “**Blocks mainline?**”; `pending scheduling` is no longer the
default state, and an unmarked task is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique
across the entire document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must
not occupy an `N.x` number).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—task id,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 digits), and issue number, when one exists—on one
line: `- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not write
the fix, criterion chain, gate values, file line numbers, test names, or review conclusions**: those
belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a kanban board, not a process
diary. **Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “user decision A/B/C,” “option
A,” “option B,” and “the final implementation is…” must not appear here. The board answers only “is
it complete?”; consult commit messages and the RFC-039 decision register for adjudications and
outcomes.

**Short hashes are determined after push**: a closure row contains the short hash on `origin/dev`
after the push completes. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then write the
closure row** (see “commit hash is obtained after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself carries no
hash—self-reference is impossible.

**Count columns contain numbers only**: the level-1/2/3 counts under “Scope and Positioning” contain
only current values; increment/decrement history (`+1 = …`) does not belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Resolution                                                                                                                                      |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps**. RFC defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how to perform the split; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one `annotations.rs` entry, the only mention in the entire batch.                                                                                     | P5’s steps are supplied by this document (see below).                                                                                           |
| G2  | **The three `include!` conversions have three owners and no implementation**. RFC lists them under P4; `02` assigns them to itself; `06` S7 also lists them. Yet `02`’s change list (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**.                                                                                                                                   | Implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 in this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC and `06` now point here.                |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts**. `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists four scripts + one `cargo test`; `07` lists four differently named checks; `04` also listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least nine new scripts and no canonical list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9. | The canonical list appears in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to that table.       |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines requiring revival,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` argues for deletion.                                                                                                                                                       | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision register C1; Pratt is no longer removed).                                                              |
| G5  | **Conflicting L2 goal wording**: RFC and the directory index previously said “grammar-driven syntax.”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | This has converged on **a declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3. |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Reason for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent parallel representations / do not
endlessly pad / do not patch when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The
rules must be established before work starts; otherwise, P1 would already be adding `mod`
declarations to `tests/mod.rs` while reviving tests—the precise cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Solution)

Source: Vulnerability-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 ＋
**Silent-discard-point audit of 2026-10-07 (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, decision of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect where “the old behavior did not count as success”—**A silent failure / B silent
> mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, silently wrong
> answer)—it **may be fixed in passing during the refactor**, but all four requirements are
> mandatory: ① red before green (the red criterion exists first and genuinely fails); ② do not
> change the externally observable behavior of programs that previously compiled successfully and
> ran correctly (they must not become failures, and existing diagnostic codes/text/exit codes must
> not be changed or removed); ③ register in the same commit (mark the error type on this row + add a
> phase revision note + include the “Error Type” line in the PR’s required block); ④ regenerate the
> baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible semantics / E external
> contract tables / F RFC-level design changes still require prior adjudication. For the expanded
> criteria and A–F whitelist, see
> [07 §Semantic-Correction Routing Criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md); the “default
> super-refactor + post-hoc registration” approach is not adopted** (reason: RFC-039 D59: without a
> red criterion, fixes cannot be distinguished from regressions, conflicting with both “no C5′
> exists” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

**Acceptance**: vulnerability criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn
them red again**. **Risk**: adding E4018 to a multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must first have red criteria (changing code first is forbidden);
3.4.3 requires manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 follow C2/C3 and the P9 9.2 gate. **Risk**: the new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus differential-baseline
and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) may proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects (such as
> `Sorted(3)` silently passing) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure work. 3.3
> (panic-to-diagnostic) has no prerequisite and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Auto-Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**; it is distinct from P10 S5’s “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust’s
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps the rewrite
surface of all four refactor phases; reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                               | Files                                                                                                              | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and syntax branches                                         | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexical convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                     |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                              |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the pub branches of `collect_exports`       | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!` → real `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**; pub branches are moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                                  |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (slim down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `semantic_tokens`’s `Public` modifier                               | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ir_gen`’s `is_pub`-ignoring binding                                | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 31 `pub` occurrences in `src/std/`                                  | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase modifies them directly, but **P6’s hard acceptance criterion requires no difference in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; direct-driver tests under `tests/` are exempt—see P6’s hard acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Incidental benefit**: 029g deletes the dead `env.exports` table (filled by the producer and never
consumed anywhere) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4’s 4.3 obligation ledger loses
one “produced but never consumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must first land a red criterion before
   code is changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced
   top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (pub items were previously always
   exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` test case in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, replace them with equivalent new
   cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` all pass.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial, not
parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not depend on 3.4;
implementers choose which to start based on available context.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: this section’s adoption (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) was included in `97071c81b` during a parallel-stream cleanup of the
> working tree; that commit’s message records “3.4 supplementary registration + D57/D58 decision
> filing” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten. Following the established
> convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation note), it is registered in place
> as a post-hoc bisection reference.

|                                            | 4.9.9 Named-argument calls to a cross-unit single-definition method **lose the formal-name table** (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during 7c closure): calling a cross-unit (registry-injected) method with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named-argument calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (the old behavior was not success: named arguments were silently dropped, followed by runtime failure or silently wrong value). **Scope (final form after two narrowing rounds on 2026-11-26—add only three items; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—using the defining unit’s qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]`, obtain declaration-time formal names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (candidate ↔ mixed-IR name ↔ formal name as three co-ordered vectors, using the same data as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) looks up the name table using the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name`, not two bare names. These two locations fix **only bare-name imports** (`local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate-injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (skip when `local != target`), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**Class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “same input, multiple results” caused by HashMap iteration order**, not a fix of the original bug; criterion = same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is allowed per method key; removing ascending-order merge produces two results). **Criterion (red before green)**: driver-level `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs`, 2 cases (bare import with one candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; file header records the history gate); unit `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (`method_param_info` empty-name-table guard ⇒ None, non-empty table returned unchanged); unit `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the determinism criterion above). Project fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (`alias-overload` fixture is deleted along with the alias-surface retirement); corpus differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` is now 404 lines: **relative to direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (an intermediate state contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 basic fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered final history). The line-count change = an unavoidable consequence of fixture entry/exit (`corpus_probe` regenerated and byte-identical to the committed baseline), **not lost coverage**. **Known gaps (named individually; old behavior = silently ignored or silently dropped; D60② “should report but does not,” Class A)**: closure value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / built-in container constructors other than `len` named arguments / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two entries are corrected according to P0’s measurement semantics**: ① **static function shapes** (both intra-unit and cross-unit, definition-style and binding-style) are **entirely unavailable today**—intra-unit `check` reports E3006, cross-unit definition-style `run` reports E6007, and cross-unit binding-style `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code, so this is unrelated to named arguments and is not “named arguments are silently dropped”; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments fail similarly** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006); the root cause is that the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table, also unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 Class A fixed in passing: the old behavior E6007/E1014 was not success, so no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (receiver type inferred and not written in the annotation). These previously produced, respectively, runtime E6007 with silently dropped arguments and compile-time `E1014 (available: )` false rejection; all now bind by declaration-time formal name (value assertion 6.0; criterion `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in that file’s header history gate). Two identity-surface residuals remain, one closed: the unit’s own same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot register the unit’s own declaration) **has been closed with the 4.9.10-S2a import-surface work** (project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is green); the remaining one: function-body-level/cross-scope imports are merged globally per unit (shared import table)—this shape itself does not work (an existing defect: check passes, run reports E6006), was not introduced by this batch, and is not fixed. **Deletions in this round (relative to the first six rounds of 4.9.9)**: candidate-provider priority, candidate-signature comparison, owner/compatibility inference, the `frontend::module::import_face` shared-provider table, the IR-side “no name table ⇒ E1014” fallback, and the **E5006 ambiguity prohibition at the import-name resolution point**—the latter rejected mixed/alias-only shapes that previously ran on the parent commit (Class D), and was withdrawn by the 2026-11-26 decision; this round introduces no new ambiguity determination. **Visible changes**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (**bare-name imports**, including two-candidate overloads) change from E1014 with an empty table to binding by name (measured 6.0 / 30); **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, `checker.rs` **must** add
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so the import remains unchanged; as measured, 5.3 **did not migrate
it**, so this batch adds no re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines—this
increases navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and provides zero decoupling benefit. The remaining
submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) await the files growing back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified term world**—type positions and value positions share
> one compile-time term system. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **only input** to slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> decision** (identical after normalizing both sides; does not bind type variables); evidence is the
> **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value environment/single-value
> pinning/Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (holding for closed terms and
> open/recursive terms); Σ construction points **reuse the same evidence interface** and do not
> establish another one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not merely that subphase
> names are checked off.**

> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and completed; F4 adjudication → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans typecheck→mono, while d leans types/solver→sema), and C.2 may
> run in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (does not depend on defeq); D implementation waits
> for confirmation of the B design package; it depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and
> may depend on the typed exit in 6.9.3. **P7 gate = exits of A/B/C; D does not block.**

> **Prerequisite for A.C3: F4 adjudication (A adjudicated, 2026-11-16; measurement)**: the old
> wording “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly`
> have been deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no
> request is created, and the representation layer’s `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold
> `k-1`. **The adjudication changes to two orthogonal decisions plus one termination subdecision**:
> D-a representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: no
> specialization); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1 second field and C-2 reconstruction from IR
> both break the single representation/evaluator, C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive firing
> pushes the recursion chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a fold within the instance / T-b
> bounded firing + fallback to the original at the boundary / T-c a termination layer or spec
> change). **Do A first, then adjudicate; before measurement, “A is implementable” must not be
> treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3
> implementation is a separate task and does not claim complete I4.**

> **Prerequisite for B.d: decision-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 requires the
> decision point to use unification first; after unification fails, equivalence may be attempted,
> but the partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back. The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (contain no unbound
> variables); what are the snapshot/restoration boundaries and costs; and do unify and defeq share
> one budget or have separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq decides only equivalence and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; the wiring contract in 6.9.3c has already wasted
> two rounds because it assumed `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has
> zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ error-code generator idempotence (if emission points/code tables change); and
> ④ classification under D59 plus red-before-green for behavioral changes. **Wiring tasks have
> additional requirements**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many
> paths, which are reachable); unit-test reachability must not be passed off as user reachability;
> rollback and budget must have measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537 (Class D,
> proof-function formal refinement is silently discarded; do not fix before adjudication, and
> 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; a Class C boundary, and if not
> closed, 6.9.4 covers only module-local forms), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow;
> **closed**—3.20.30 was closed on 2026-11-14: 64MB large-stack thread at the orchestration layer +
> parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall;
> **closed**—on 2026-11-16, three sites entered and exited together: `call_form_is_rewritten` /
> `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` via the single point
> `rewritten_call_target`, covering `Call`/`TailCall`, with init sections and function bodies
> sharing one site-rewriting source; red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer;
> **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + both post-mono entry points connected + C2c temporary
> avoidance removed; red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and deviations), #552 (imported
> multi-parameter predicate proof execution; a 6.9.5 neighbor, separate task). **Ownership pending
> adjudication**: the four open-constraint tripwires in `rfc027_refined_transparency` (`Eq(N, n)`)
> do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equality bridge; leave them in 6.9.4 outOfScope or move them to
> 6.9.1/E4018’s proof-function surface, subject to adjudication.

> **Do not claim / boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim complete Π/Σ; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and does not
> fulfill open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwires; `f(y)(y)`’s second value position is not part of this
> item; witness erasure ≠ Runtime check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 cover only forms
> that do not depend on proof-function formal refinement; if #539 is not fixed, 6.9.4 covers only
> module-local forms; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 landed (2026-11-19); 2.1.4’s inner-isolation
> red was cleared on 2026-11-20 (criterion rewritten around slot identity in the 2.1.4 closure) ⇒
> all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a gate are removed.

**Hard acceptance** (**wording revised on 2026-10-27, following the 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-driver test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive changed code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) **may be modified when mechanically required by the change**,
but each modification must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be
deleted and assertions must not be relaxed**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch
(new diagnostic code + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: the original wording (2026-10-26 decision ②) said
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, treating all of `tests/` as zero-diff; the revised wording
> **changes only direct-driver test files from “zero diff” to “may be changed but must register file
> / line count / reason”**; the zero-diff requirement for the **corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`),
> baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library (`src/std/`)** remains unchanged. First
> application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed by **3 lines** (2
> `assert_format_eq` changes from `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), reason = the assertion’s expected
> type name must be synchronized with the changed spelling; no tests were deleted and no assertions
> were relaxed. See “P6 6.1 Name Normalization Closure.”

> whole and merging statements belong to the full migration and are outside this batch, with a
> separate design round after P7. `synth.rs` is a new boundary, not a move, and belongs to 7c.1.

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and missing a consumer will **silently change
associativity** (no error, only a different parse result). Defenses are permanent D1–D3 assertions
and operator-property cross-checking tests; new operators must enter both the table and the
cross-check tests.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code refers backward to `sema`, `check-boundary.py` will block it.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelism

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects is not blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure work; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver
> requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must first be written as failing (2.4.1/2.4.3), and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to be frozen into the stage table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)’s deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (see the list in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` conversion and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, otherwise regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representation does not converge first, the new IR grows into a third representation; **P7 gate = exits of 6.9 phases A/B/C** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and 6.9.4 complete), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface and must not establish a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a prerequisite for P7 and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume an undecided defeq/quantifier interface |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count take their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### Parallel Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                            |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert by file                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three criterion layers are independent                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                             |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be captured last                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` sites under `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (same
B6/E5 batch files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**New internal document constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move prerequisite for P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm must
precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”; only the
  D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole canonical list of CI scripts**—the three coexisting lists in original gap G3 made
  closure impossible. This table merges them into 10 active scripts, each owned by one phase (9.8
  was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and hardening points explicitly
  traceable.
- **P3.5 adopts RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to execute after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as adopting `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status corrections into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker splitting would exceed the rollback granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “fixed defects must
  not be rolled back,” without requiring a record of what was fixed. **Execution convention**: every
  1.3.x fix’s commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect description as a post-hoc
  bisection reference.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two
  exclusive commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 renaming references, and missing one
  **silently changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, with deletion left
  in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally intended as an “independent issue”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: `2341` was adopted as 7e.3; `2315` was revalidated on 2026-11-28 as an
  audit false positive (the field has no producer, and the language layer has no throw/try/catch),
  7e.2 was cancelled, and exception remnants moved to P10 S6.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into the
  generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

## Conflict Register: All Adjudicated

> **The original “Conflict Register” C1–C8 and all open questions in the individual documents have
> converged into the [RFC-039 Decision Register](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** No pending items remain in this document. Item-by-item mapping:

| Original ID | Issue                                                                               | Decision                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1          | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                           | **Revive it** (P1’s premise is that revived tests contain real assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                   |
| C2          | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs table-driven implementation                          | **Fallback option**: retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + cross-checking the two `BinOp` sets against the same source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3          | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification                   | **S1 belongs to C6** (revival does not require an equivalence oracle, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                  |
| C4          | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                        | **No whitelist**; the difference set must be empty. If it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                            |
| C5          | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 lists this as a mandatory verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                  |
| C6          | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                                 | **The wasm-path vulnerability fix is merged into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                         |
| C7          | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Belongs to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                         |
| C8          | `upvalue_count` correction and `.42` version number                                 | **Fix it + raise `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                       |
